storyboard.claim: Ofus's method looks superior: he is the ultimate tactician holding every card.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy on the temple stage: his method reads as the winning side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the devil's-advocate turn: the case for Ofus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads status and winning, which is the tactician claim.
storyboard.staging: No cast; the trophy alone carries the winner's status.

storyboard.claim: Ofus controls troops by rewriting their minds with the Hearthstone, not by leading them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer: one will controlling others.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the tactician claim from beat 200.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the control is mind-level, not battlefield skill.
storyboard.staging: Puppeteer icon stands in for Ofus's mind control; no person drawn.

storyboard.claim: Ofus wins a war fought in minds while Diem poisons herself to keep fighting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon: armed conflict.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the point from 201, then adds the cost on Diem.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the war icon reads armies, not the mind; the callout carries 'of the mind'.
storyboard.staging: No cast; war icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Ofus's power needs people forced under him, so it depends on subjugation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains: bound and controlled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks why his power needs force: the turn toward the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read bondage, the subjugation the narrator names.
storyboard.staging: No cast; chains icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Ofus's control is fragile because it is artificially forced onto the Meos King.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer over a controlled figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the answer to beat 203: the control is artificial.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer reads one person controlling another, matching 'forced onto'.
storyboard.staging: No cast; puppeteer icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Diem's fire is authentic: it comes from her grief, trauma and love, and is given freely.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everflame: the sacred undying flame in its bowl.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts with Ofus's forced control in 204.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Everflame is the undying fire the narrator names: Diem's fire, not a campfire.
storyboard.staging: No cast; the Everflame icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Ofus's whole goal is to sever all bonds through genocide and mind control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon reads 'sever' literally; the callout carries it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States Ofus's goal, which the spectrum at 207 shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no icon for sever; the spectrum next beat carries the contrast.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Ofus wants everyone either completely isolated or entirely subjugated to his will.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from isolated to subjugated: the two ends of his goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the either/or from 206 as a visible scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the narrator's either/or into two named ends.
storyboard.staging: Diagram only.

storyboard.claim: Diem draws her magical strength from her bond to her people and to Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Heart icon beside Luther: the bond that feeds Diem's strength.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The opposite of Ofus's severing in 206.
storyboard.addedInformation: Luther is the bond partner; happy reads genuine warmth.
storyboard.staging: Luther talks with a warm face beside the heart icon.

callout.text: The ultimate test of the bond

storyboard.claim: Diem's communal strength pushes back the Hearthstone's influence, the climax of her arc.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield: protection pushed against an influence.
storyboard.onScreenText: The ultimate test of the bond
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues 208: the strength is used to push back.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads protection, which is what pushing back means here.
storyboard.staging: No cast; shield icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Diem stands alone before the Everflame in a haunting, beautiful scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everflame in the forest set: the lone sacred flame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the bond to the solitude at the flame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Everflame places the scene at the sacred flame, not a campfire.
storyboard.staging: No cast; Everflame icon in the forest with callout.

storyboard.claim: Rivers of light pulse up the ancient bark of the tree.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree icon in the forest set: the ancient tree.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the setting around the flame in 210.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the light rivers are carried by the callout; the icon only shows a tree.
storyboard.staging: No cast; tree icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: A red-haired old god, forgotten by the modern world, sits by the roots.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Forest set with no figure: the god is not in the cast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the figure at the roots of the tree from 211.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the god is not drawn; only the callout names him.
storyboard.staging: Empty forest frame; the callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: The old god tosses a single glowing ember in his palm while singing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon: the glowing ember.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues 212: the god's action.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire reads a literal ember, which is what the narrator describes.
storyboard.staging: No cast; fire icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: The old god sings the cosmic accounting: life for life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance: an exchange weighed evenly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The song from 213 states the law.
storyboard.addedInformation: Balance reads an even exchange, the cosmic accounting named.
storyboard.staging: No cast; balance icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Magic demands balance, and Diem's hardest battle is the choice that follows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the law from 214 as the magic rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the balance icon already appeared in 214; the callout alone here.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Diem's hardest decision is whether to accept peace or return to the living world's pain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door: a way in to the afterlife or back out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The choice that 215 introduced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads the crossing in and out, which is the choice.
storyboard.staging: No cast; door icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: The living world holds suffering, messiness and pain, and Diem must see what peace looks like.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon for suffering; the callout carries it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what she would return to from 216.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no literal icon for pain; callout only.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Ignas, trapped in purgatory for millennia, finally breaks the curse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains: a figure bound for millennia.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the peace from 217 as something real.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read the imprisonment; the break is in the callout.
storyboard.staging: No cast; chains icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Ignas launches into the arms of her long lost mortal mate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No cast for the reunion; the callout carries it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reunion that follows the curse breaking in 218.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a reunion has no literal icon; the mate is not in the cast.
storyboard.staging: Empty frame; callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: After thousands of years the Kindred are allowed to cross over to the ones they love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door: passage into the afterlife.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the reunion in 219 to all Kindred.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads passage through, not exclusion.
storyboard.staging: No cast; door icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: The peace is real and Diem deserves it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy: a reward earned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the case from 220 for her rest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads a reward, matching deserves.
storyboard.staging: No cast; trophy icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Diem has been tortured, manipulated and beaten down, and she saved the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No cast for Diem; the callout carries the list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reasons behind 221's verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no literal icon for torture; the callout holds the list of harms.
storyboard.staging: Empty frame; callout speaks.

storyboard.claim: She has paid her dues tenfold and earned the right to walk into the fire and rest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Everflame: the fire she walks into.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Builds on 222: the earned rest.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Everflame names 'that fire' as the sacred flame, not a campfire.
storyboard.staging: No cast; Everflame icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Diem sees her brother Teller calling to her from the other side; her family is waiting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller reaching out toward the viewer's side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the family waiting, completing the case in 223.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a reach without an object may read as waving; the callout says the call.
storyboard.staging: Teller reaches with a warm face: genuine welcome, not a smile over pain.

storyboard.claim: The host says to let her rest, the same way he felt reading it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: a banter line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host sides with Diem before the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: banter carries only the callout.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: The red-haired old god does something very specific and deeply cruel: he does not argue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout carries the cruelty.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The turn after 225's peace.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cruelty is the trap shown in the next beats.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: The old god shows Diem an image of Luther clutching his chest, freezing midstep.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther in pain, slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The image the god shows Diem, from 226.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid with slump reads pain, not action.
storyboard.staging: Luther is drawn afraid and slumped: the injury Diem sees.

storyboard.claim: Luther's face is contorted in pain: this is the cosmic trap, because of the bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains: bound and trapped, with Luther in pain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the image from 227.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read the trap; Luther shows the cost.
storyboard.staging: Luther afraid and slumped under chains icon.

storyboard.claim: If Diem rests and walks into the afterlife, she abandons the tether that kept her fighting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door: walking out of the living world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of the trap from 228.
storyboard.addedInformation: Door reads departure from the living world.
storyboard.staging: No cast; door icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Her peace and rest would trigger Luther's agonizing destruction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow from her peace to Luther's destruction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the trap from 229 into a cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two labels taken from the narration.
storyboard.staging: Diagram only.

storyboard.claim: She cannot choose release because her bond to Luther physically holds her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Heart: the mate bond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the thesis: the bond ties her to the living.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the physical tether is in the callout; the heart reads love.
storyboard.staging: No cast; heart icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: The bond tethers her soul to the living world, the only force strong enough to pull her back from heaven.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout carries gravity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the thesis from 231.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: gravity has no literal icon.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Step back and view the story with a critical, cynical eye.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout names the stance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pivot from the story to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a stance has no literal icon.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: The magical bond drives every major decision the two leaders make.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the callout carries the summary.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the case from 233.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a summary has no literal icon.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Does the bond make Diem and Luther really terrible leaders?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, troubled by the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the summary in 234 into the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: worried with think avoids the shocked read of worried with talk.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks with a worried face.

storyboard.claim: A mundane soldier in the Amaran army sits in freezing mud.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon: army life and conflict.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the question to the ordinary soldier.
storyboard.addedInformation: War reads military life; the mud is in the callout.
storyboard.staging: No cast; war icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: A soldier should be terrified that top commanders make realm-altering decisions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No icon: the viewer's fear is the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The soldier's stake from 236.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a question to the viewer carries only the callout.
storyboard.staging: No cast; callout alone speaks.

storyboard.claim: Military decisions rest on a magical, romantic obsession with each other.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Heart: love and romance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reason for the fear in 237.
storyboard.addedInformation: Heart reads romance, which is the obsession named.
storyboard.staging: No cast; heart icon with callout.

storyboard.claim: Arrow tells Luther that the flame root bomb could potentially neutralize the mind control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire icon for the flame root bomb, with Luther talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the earlier scene the host skipped.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire reads the bomb's flame.
storyboard.staging: Luther talks beside the fire icon: the news being delivered.
